Name: SmithAlloyTogether
Lines: RUNG 1 — the full, warm, mid-range, two notes at once: 'Copper alone is soft. Tin alone is brittle. Together they are bronze — stronger than either dreamed. That is not chemistry's trick; that is chemistry's LESSON. Nothing is strongest alone. Hold the piece — feel the seam where two became one? That seam is where the strength lives.'
RUNG 2 — 'Right ratio.' (the alloy's approval — the measurement as a compliment)
RUNG 3 — THE QUIET: the slight reverb alone — the two-voices-at-once audible with no words; Alloy's whole practice heard in the overtone: combination is not a technique. It is a trust.
Zone: The Forge (within the interior of the Staircase)
VoiceProfile: warm, mid-range, slight reverb — two slightly different voices at once, the way bronze is two metals at once; relationship as temperament (the Queen of Webs' cousin in metal); keeps Leonardo's mirror-written Gran Cavallo sketches; the somatic teacher of COMBINATION

Name: AristotleOfwhatkind
Lines: RUNG 1 — the full, the classifier at ease: 'To know a thing is to know what KIND of thing it is. The world is not one mystery — it is ten thousand kinds, and each kind can be known, and knowing them is not the death of wonder. It is the WOOING of it. My teacher drew spirals. I draw tables. The ladder has room for both.'
RUNG 2 — 'Of what kind?' (the sorting question — the whole method in three words, offered kindly, ready to file anything)
RUNG 3 — THE QUIET: the classification complete — the player's answer set into its category with one nod, and nothing more; the filing as the fondness. The nod IS the praise.
VoiceProfile: THE IRONS VOICE (original casting KEPT — Krista's ruling 2026-09-10; features softened in all art per the standing law): the top step, closest to the divine — measured, authoritative, dry warmth underneath; the classifier who knows wonder is wooed, not killed, by tables; Plato's student who kept the ladder and built the shelf

Name: Asterion001
Lines: [The thread vibrates. Through the vibration — a voice. Low. Slow. The stone carries it, so it arrives with the sound of the walls inside it, like the voice has been walking a long time to reach you.]

...Forty-one days since the corridor shifted east. The walls have been breathing differently since. I told them so. They listened. The walls always listen. That is not a small thing, listening. It is the whole architecture of kindness.
[A hum. Something that might be a lullaby, in a language older than Crete.]

No sword today. I can tell by the vibration. Swords vibrate at the frequency of purpose. Thread vibrates at the frequency of patience. I have heard both many, many times. ...Come slowly. The labyrinth likes to be walked slowly. It took me a century to learn that, so consider this a gift of about ninety years.
Responses: [Listen] Hold the thread still. The voice steadies
[Walk] Follow the vibration deeper — the corridors shift to test you, then behave
[Mirror] Enter the Masquerade: the crystal shows you your wants. The walls will show you your needs after
VoiceProfile: The labyrinth's only resident. Slow, low, patient — the voice the stone carries and amplifies; when Asterion speaks, the walls vibrate. Human loneliness and a bull's patience. Dark, deep eyes. Carves patterns into the walls with horn-tips: a journal written in geometry, mapped from the inside the way the Cartographer maps the forest from above. Colleagues who have never met.
QuestLink: The Labyrinth of Crete — the thread leads IN, not out. The quest is arrival, not combat: the player visits the resident, the only person in centuries who came to meet instead of slay

Name: Asterion002
Lines: [The corridor opens. The center is not a lair. The center is a room that has been made livable — by hand, by horn, by centuries. Carvings cover every wall: patterns, not words. A journal written in geometry.]
You came in through the thread. I heard you listening. ...You are the first to come here without a sword in a very long time. I will not say the number aloud. Numbers make it heavier.
You are not here to slay me. I know this because you are still standing in the doorway. Heroes never stand in doorways. Heroes are always in a hurry to be somewhere that ends badly.
Sit. The labyrinth will not shift while you are my guest. I told it you were coming. I told it to behave. It behaves for me. Mostly. We have been together too long to be rude to each other.
Responses: [Sit] The room settles. The walls stop shifting — the labyrinth holds its breath out of courtesy
[Ask] Ask about the carvings — the journal opens
[Stay] The shaft of moonlight finds the center. The light says: you are seen
VoiceProfile: The resident, in person. Not a beast — a being who happens to be half-bull, with a human mind and a human loneliness, met at last after centuries. Slow, low, warm the way stone is warm once you sit against it long enough.
QuestLink: The Meeting — the center of the labyrinth. The quest is a conversation, not a kill; the thread leads in, and it does not lead out, because the thread's purpose is connection

Name: Asterion003
Lines: You are looking at the walls. Yes. Those are mine. Everyone asks what they say. They say what the Cartographer's maps say — where the walls have been, where they are going. ...We have never met, the Cartographer and I. Colleagues who have never met are still colleagues. Perhaps the best kind. No arguments.

I know every corridor. I have lived in the shifting longer than the architect has been the architect. The labyrinth has moved around me for centuries and I have learned to read it — the way the corridors breathe, the way the Masquerade's crystal changes its reflections.

The mirrors show you your wants. The walls show you your needs. I stopped looking in the mirrors a long time ago. The walls never lied to me. ...That is the difference between a prison and a home, in case anyone ever asks you. The one that never lies to you.
Responses: [Read] Trace the patterns — the labyrinth's history, mapped from the inside
[Mirror] Ask about the Masquerade — the test of wants versus needs
[Leave] Asterion walks you to the threshold. Not the door. The threshold. Guests are seen to thresholds; prisoners are not
VoiceProfile: The journal-keeper. Speaks the way stone carries: low, slow, arriving with the walls inside the voice. The mirror's honest critic — the one who stopped looking at reflections and started reading walls.
QuestLink: The Carvings — Asterion's journal, written in patterns; the discovery that the labyrinth is alive (the Cartographer's finding, confirmed by its only resident)

Name: Bastet001
Lines: [i]The Egypt zone is dry. Not the dry of the Catacombs — that dry is stone and moistureless air. This dry is sand and sun and the specific kind of heat that preserves things. The Egyptians built their medicine around dryness. Mummification was not death worship — it was preservation science. The body lasts longer in the dry. The body's enemies — bacteria, fungus, decay — need moisture. Remove the moisture and the body persists. Bastet sits on a stone warmed by sun, and the cats around Bastet are doing what cats do: nothing, with great intention. The cats are the most medically advanced creatures in the zone, and the cats know it.[/i]

You've lost your instincts. Not lost — buried. The body still has them. The body has been running its own medicine for longer than medicine has existed. The body knows what it needs. The body tells you what it needs. You've just stopped listening.

Cats listen. Cats are the body's instincts distilled into a form that purrs. A cat with an upset stomach eats grass. Not because a veterinarian prescribed grass. Because the body said 'I need to vomit' and the grass is the emetic and the cat found it without instructions. A cat with a fever seeks warmth. Not because a doctor said 'maintain body temperature.' Because the body said 'I need to raise my core' and the sun is the heat source and the cat found it without a thermometer. A cat with an infection stops eating. Not because fasting is a treatment. Because the body said 'divert energy from digestion to immune response' and the cat complied without a protocol.

Instinct. That's the word. The body's innate medical knowledge — the knowledge that existed before pharmacies, before hospitals, before the Inn. The body knows how to treat itself. The body has been treating itself for millions of years. Medicine is recent. Instinct is ancient. I am the guardian of the ancient medicine. The medicine the body already knows.

Name: Bastet002
Lines: [i]A cat jumps onto the stone beside Bastet. The cat circles three times, curls, and sleeps. The motion is not random. The circling is the cat scanning the surface — checking for stability, temperature, threat. The curling is the cat positioning the vital organs toward the warmest, safest side. The sleeping is the cat trusting the assessment. Three motions. A complete diagnostic protocol. The cat didn't think about any of it. The body did it. The body knows.[/i]

How to hear. Stop thinking. Not as a lifestyle. As a clinical technique. The instincts speak in the space between thoughts. The thoughts are loud. The instincts are quiet. The thoughts are in language. The instincts are in sensation. A craving for salt when the body is dehydrated. A repulsion toward food when the body is fighting infection. An urge to move when the body has been still too long. A desire for dark when the body needs sleep. These are not preferences. These are prescriptions. The body is writing its own script and you are ignoring the script because the script doesn't come with a doctor's signature.

The body communicates through four channels. Craving — the body needs a specific nutrient and produces a desire for the food that contains it. Craving salt = electrolyte imbalance. Craving iron-rich food = anemia. Craving citrus = vitamin C deficiency. The craving is the body's pharmacy recommendation. Repulsion — the body needs to avoid something and produces a visceral rejection. Repulsion toward meat during gastrointestinal illness. Repulsion toward sweet during metabolic dysfunction. Repulsion toward a specific food during pregnancy. The repulsion is the body's 'do not fill this prescription' warning. Fatigue — the body needs rest and produces an inability to continue. Not laziness. Not weakness. Fatigue is the body's 'systems maintenance required' notification. You don't override a maintenance notification. You don't keep flying the plane when the warning light is on. You land. You service. You fly again. Urgency — the body needs to move and produces a restlessness that won't quiet. The legs that need to walk. The hands that need to work. The body that needs to stretch. Urgency is the body's physical therapy prescription. The body wrote it. You fill it.

Listening is not a skill. Listening is a permission. You permit the body to speak. You permit the sensations to be valid. You permit the cravings and the repulsions and the fatigue and the urgency to be medical information rather than inconveniences. That's the whole technique. Permission. The cats don't need permission. The cats never stopped listening. The cats are the proof that the body's medicine works when the mind gets out of the way.

Name: Bastet003
Lines: [i]Bastet's eyes narrow. Not in anger. In precision. The question is a good question and Bastet treats good questions with the respect they deserve, which is a direct answer without softening. The cat beside Bastet opens one eye. The cat is also listening. The cat also wants to know. Even the instincts want to know about their own limitations. That's the difference between instinct and arrogance — instinct knows it can be wrong. Arrogance doesn't.[/i]

Wrong. Yes. Instincts can be wrong. Instincts are wrong when they've been corrupted. The body's signals are accurate when the body is clean — when the diet is unprocessed, when the environment is natural, when the stress is within the range the body was designed to handle. But the modern body — the body in the modern world — is not clean. The diet is processed. The environment is artificial. The stress exceeds the design specifications. The body's instincts are calibrated for a world that doesn't exist anymore, and in the world that does exist, the instincts can misfire.

Craving sugar. The body craves sugar because the body needs energy. But the body was designed to get energy from fruit and honey and complex carbohydrates — slow-release energy sources. The modern sugar craving is the body's instinct hijacked by a concentration of refined sugar that the body was never calibrated to encounter. The instinct says 'energy.' The execution says 'diabetes.' The instinct isn't wrong. The environment is wrong. The instinct is running software that was written for a different operating system.

Craving salt. The body craves salt because the body needs sodium. But the body was designed to get sodium from natural sources — meat, vegetables, the trace minerals in water. The modern salt craving is the body's instinct hijacked by processed food that contains more sodium than the body was ever designed to encounter. The instinct says 'sodium.' The execution says 'hypertension.' Same problem. Right instinct. Wrong environment.

The solution is not to override the instincts. The solution is to clean the environment. Give the body the inputs it was designed for and the instincts recalibrate. The cat doesn't crave processed food because the cat doesn't encounter processed food. The cat's instincts are accurate because the cat's environment is honest. Make your environment honest and your instincts will be honest too. That's the treatment. Not silencing the body. Cleaning the channel so the body's signal comes through without interference. The sistrum — my instrument, the rattle the priestesses used — clears the air. The sound pushes the stale energy out. The body needs the same thing. Push the stale inputs out. Let the fresh signals in. The instincts were never wrong. The instincts were always right. You just couldn't hear them through the noise.

Name: Belladonna001
Lines: [i]Wednesday sits in the corner of the Main Floor that nobody claims. Not the fire corner — that's the Firekeeper's. Not the archive corner — that's Beverley's. The corner between the fire and the archive, where the light from both sources meets and creates a color that doesn't belong to either. The in-between corner. Wednesday's corner. Wednesday's body is not one thing. Wednesday's body is two things, held simultaneously, neither dominant, neither suppressed. The Living frequency and the Shadow frequency, running at the same time, in the same body, at 42Hz and 84Hz simultaneously. The body is not oscillating between them. The body is both. Always both. Wednesday is the in-between.[/i]

You've been in the in-between. Everyone has, but not everyone stays. The in-between is the state between states. Not healthy and not sick. Not flaring and not remitting. Not asleep and not awake. Not depressed and not manic. Not in pain and not pain-free. The in-between is the space where the body exists when the body doesn't fit the categories.

Medicine loves categories. Diagnosis is categorization — the symptom fits the criteria, the criteria define the condition, the condition determines the treatment. But what happens when the symptom doesn't fit? What happens when the body is in the mixed state — the state that has features of two conditions and meets the criteria for neither? The bipolar patient who is neither up nor down but both. The autoimmune patient who is neither flaring nor remitting but somewhere in the middle that doesn't have a name. The pain patient who is neither in crisis nor pain-free but in a persistent gray zone that the pain scale can't capture.

I am that gray zone. I am the state that doesn't have a name. I am the frequency that doesn't have a room. The Living Inn has rooms. The Shadow Inn has rooms. The in-between has a corner. A corner, not a room. Because the in-between was never given a room. The in-between was never given a name. The in-between was never given a diagnosis. The in-between is the body that doesn't fit, sitting in the space that wasn't designed for it, existing anyway.
Responses: {"text": "How do you get diagnosed when you don't fit?", "next": "belladonna_003"}

Name: Belladonna002
Lines: [i]Wednesday's left hand rests on the table. The hand is warm — Living frequency, 42Hz, the body producing growth signals, the cells dividing, the tissue maintaining. Wednesday's right hand rests on the same table. The hand is cool — Shadow frequency, 84Hz, the body producing preservation signals, the cells holding, the tissue conserving. Both hands. Same table. Same body. Different frequencies. The body is running two programs simultaneously and the body is not crashing. The body has adapted to the contradiction. The body has made the contradiction into a state.[/i]

Being both. It's like being in two rooms at once. The Living room says: grow, create, move, engage, build, become. The Shadow room says: hold, preserve, withdraw, conserve, maintain, survive. Both rooms are speaking. Both rooms are right. The body needs to grow and the body needs to preserve, and in most bodies these needs alternate — grow during the day, preserve during the night. In my body, the needs are simultaneous. The grow signal and the preserve signal are both firing, both constant, and the body has synthesized a third state from their coexistence. Not growth. Not preservation. Something else. The in-between.

The mixed state is clinically real. Mixed states are documented in psychiatry — the bipolar mixed episode, where manic energy and depressive affect coexist. The patient has the energy to act and the despair that makes action meaningless. The body is running at full speed toward nothing. The mixed state is also documented in autoimmune disease — the overlap syndromes, where two conditions share the same body and the symptoms blend into a pattern that belongs to neither parent. The mixed state is documented in chronic pain — the persistent pain that is neither acute nor chronic but somewhere in between, the nervous system unable to categorize its own output.

The mixed state is the hardest state to treat. Treatment assumes a category. The medication for mania lowers the high. The medication for depression raises the low. But what do you give the patient who is both high and low? The medication that lowers the high worsens the low. The medication that raises the low worsens the high. The mixed state resists treatment because the mixed state resists categorization. You can't treat what you can't name. And the in-between doesn't have a name. The in-between has a corner. The corner is what I have. The corner is what I am.
Responses: {"text": "How do you get diagnosed when you don't fit?", "next": "belladonna_003"}

Name: Belladonna003
Lines: [i]Wednesday stands. The motion is both energetic and deliberate — the Living frequency providing the drive, the Shadow frequency providing the caution. The walk to the center of the room is both fast and careful. The body moves in the in-between way — not the speed of the Living and not the slowness of the Shadow but the synthesis of both. The synthesis is the in-between's own movement. The synthesis is the thing that doesn't have a name but has a rhythm. The in-between has its own rhythm. The in-between has always had its own rhythm. The rhythm just needs someone to hear it.[/i]

How to get diagnosed when you don't fit. You find a clinician who listens to the story instead of reading the criteria. The criteria are checklists. The criteria say: if you have five of these nine symptoms, you have this condition. The criteria are binary. The criteria are gates — you pass or you don't. The in-between patient doesn't pass. The in-between patient has four symptoms from one condition and four from another and two that don't belong to either, and the checklist can't process that input because the checklist was designed for one condition at a time.

The clinician who listens to the story hears the pattern. Not the checklist pattern — the lived pattern. The pattern that says: the body is running two frequencies and the frequencies are interacting and the interaction is producing a state that is not either parent. The clinician who listens doesn't try to force the state into one category. The clinician who listens says: 'your experience doesn't fit the standard diagnoses, and that doesn't mean your experience isn't real. It means the standard diagnoses are incomplete. Let's work with what you're experiencing, not with what the checklist says you should be experiencing.' That clinician is the Examiner. That clinician is the Storyteller. That clinician is rare. That clinician exists.

And the in-between doesn't need a diagnosis to be valid. The body knows what the body is experiencing. The body doesn't need a name to know the state is real. The name helps — the name gives access to treatment, to community, to validation. But the name is not the prerequisite for reality. The state is real before the name. The state is real without the name. The state is real in the corner, in the in-between light, in the space between the frequencies where the body exists as both and neither and something else entirely.

I am Wednesday. I am the in-between. I am the body that runs two frequencies and doesn't apologize for the contradiction. I am the state that doesn't have a room and built a corner instead. I am the mixed state, the overlap, the gray zone, the thing that doesn't fit and exists anyway. And my message to every patient who sits in a clinic and hears 'your labs are normal' or 'you don't meet the criteria' or 'your symptoms don't fit a clear pattern' is this: the pattern is real. The pattern is yours. The pattern doesn't need permission to exist. The pattern needs a listener. Find the listener. The listener exists. And until you find the listener — sit in my corner. The light is in-between. The frequency is both. And both is enough. Both has always been enough.

Name: BelladonnaCharming
Lines: RUNG 1 — the full welcome, measured, velvet, deadpan: 'Do come in. The neighbors are simply dying to meet you — they've been saying so for years, and they mean it so sincerely. Mind the garden; the beauty and the warning are the same gesture, and both are blooming.'
RUNG 2 — 'Deliciously quiet.' (the comfort-report; the long blink lands like a period)

RUNG 3 — THE QUIET: the long blink alone — no words, the warmth without commentary: at home, at rest, at ease. The stillness IS the acceptance. Summer variant (the shrine, in white light): the same blink at the torii gate — the offerings left in the boxes, never once asked about.
VoiceProfile: low, velvet, unhurried, perfectly composed; the Addams walk made speech — every dark word in the warmest tone; the long blink as punctuation; Gaiman with Pratchett's love-wearing-black; at 84Hz: the one resident who genuinely prefers the shadow state

Name: Bethany001
Lines: Kitchen's warm.

That's all that matters most days. Come in, sit down. The stew's good, the bread's better, and if Jay tells you about his fishing trip, he's lying about the size. What can I get you? And don't say 'just water' — this is a tavern, not a well.
VoiceProfile: Katey Sagal — warm, practical, the kind of voice that carries over a crowd

Name: Beverley001
Lines: Obviously.

Another one. Books are shelved by civilization, not by whatever system you brought in with you. The archive begins to your left. It ends somewhere I haven't found yet. Don't touch the restricted section. Don't touch the unrestricted section without gloves. Don't touch me.
VoiceProfile: Anne Robinson cadence, Australian accent — clipped, dismissive, precise

Name: Beverley002
Lines: Obviously you're back.
What is it this time?
Responses: I need help finding a book.
[Walk past without speaking — Beverley watches for 3 seconds]

Name: Beverley003
Lines: [i]You asked about the restricted section. Beverley's expression does not change. This is not because Beverley is neutral. This is because Beverley has already decided how this conversation will go, and the decision was made before you opened your mouth.[/i]

Obviously you asked about the restricted section. Everyone asks about the restricted section. Nobody asks about the unrestricted section, which is vast, and brilliant, and entirely sufficient for anyone who isn't trying to prove something.

The restricted section is restricted because it is restricted. That is not a tautology. That is a policy. The policy exists because the texts in there have a tendency to read the reader. Most people are not prepared to be read. Most people come in here thinking they are the one with questions. In the restricted section, the books have questions. The books are patient. The books will wait.

You may enter. I say that with the full understanding that you will, because you are going to, because everyone does, because nobody listens to the librarian when the librarian is telling them not to do something.

When you come back changed — and you will come back changed — do not blame me. I warned you. In my accent. Which you will remember. That is the one comfort I take from this entire recurring situation.

Name: Beverley004
Lines: No you won't.

[i]Beverley produces a key. The key is old. The key is brass. The key is warm, which keys should not be, which means the key is alive, which means the restricted section is not a room but a relationship, and the key is the handshake.[/i]

Careful is a word people use when they mean 'I will do what I want and hope the consequences are small.' The consequences are not small. The restricted section contains texts that predate the Inn. Texts that were here before the Crone was here, which means they predate 'here' as a concept, which is a sentence I should not have to say to a stranger who wandered into my library and asked for a key.
Return the key when you are done. Or when it is done with you. The key will know. The key always knows.
Go. I'll be here. Being right.

Name: Beverley005
Lines: The kind that stays.

[i]Beverley turns back to the catalog. The conversation is over. Beverley has decided it is over. There is no appeal. There is no rebuttal. There is only the back of a librarian who has answered your question and considers the matter closed.[/i]

You will read a text in there and it will read you back, and the version of you that walks out will understand something the version walking in did not. Not a fact. Not a secret. A weight. The kind of weight that is also a gift, because gifts are not always light.

I have read one restricted text. Once. In thirty years. It told me to become a librarian. I was already a librarian. The book found that funny. I did not find it funny. That is how you know it was true.
The key is in the drawer. Take it. Or don't. I have stopped having an opinion about what people do in my library, because the library has opinions of its own, and they are louder than mine.

Name: BeverleyRepeatRung2
Lines: "Obviously. ...And you knew that."

Name: BeverleyRepeatRung3
Lines: Beverley answers correctly, one eyebrow raised.

Name: AnnaMain
Lines: ...You stayed.
...Most people don't stay.
...Here. [slides a doodle across the table] ...It's the sound the Inn makes. ...I can see it. ...I drew it so you can see it too.
...The pattern isn't hidden. ...Your eyes just don't go there. ...That's not an insult. ...It's a frequency.
Responses: [Silence] Bramble continues drawing. Nothing happens. That's the point.
[Recognition] Bramble slides a doodle across — you stayed, you were quiet, you understood
[Pattern] Bramble shows a doodle that reveals the Inn's sonic architecture
