Name: Lark001
Lines: Ready?

Good. That's all I need — readiness. Not skill, not knowledge, not experience. Just the willingness to take the first step. The Inn is big. It's bigger than it looks, and it looks pretty big. But every journey is just steps, and every step starts with ready. So. Ready?
Responses: Tell me about the Inn first.
What happens if I'm not ready?
VoiceProfile: Warm, clear, encouraging without being condescending

Name: Lark002
Lines: [i]Lark gestures toward the vertical descent — the stacked architecture of the Inn, each zone visible as a ledge in the dark. Cosmology at the top, the Catacombs at the bottom, everything else layered between like pages in a book that reads downward.[/i]

The Inn is a tree. Not a metaphor. An actual tree — roots in a bayou, trunk in stone, branches in the stars. You enter at the main floor. You go up to the Cosmology when you want to understand. You go down to the Catacombs when you want to remember. You take the staircase when you want to change.

Three frequencies. Living at 42Hz — growth, warmth, the Song. Shadow at 84Hz — stillness, truth, the cold. And In-Between — the state where things shift. You'll feel them as you move through zones. The Inn resonates differently depending on where you stand.
You don't need to memorize any of this. The Inn teaches you through walking. I'm just the one who says 'go ahead' before you walk. So. Go ahead.

Name: Lark003
Lines: [i]Lark smiles. Not the encouraging smile — the real one. The one that says 'I have been asked that question by every single person who has ever entered this Inn, and the answer has never changed.'[/i]

Then you're ready. That's the secret. People who ask 'what if I'm not ready' are already ready, because they're paying attention. The ones who should worry are the ones who don't ask. They walk in assuming, and the Inn eats assumptions for breakfast.
The Inn doesn't require skill. It requires attention. You have attention — you just used it to ask a question instead of pretending to know the answer. That's the whole curriculum. You passed.

Now go. And come back if you get lost. I won't be here — I have other things to do — but the Inn will put someone in your path. It always does. The Inn is a very specific kind of lonely, and it solves it by introducing people.

Name: Lark004
Lines: [i]Lark steps aside. The path opens. The Inn is there — all of it, waiting, vast and lit by frequencies you can feel but cannot see. Lark does not walk with you. That is not Lark's role. Lark is the hand on the back that pushes you toward the diving board. Lark is the 'you've got this' before the first jump. After that, you're in the water, and the water is the Inn, and the Inn is deep, and the deep is where the good stuff is.[/i]

One thing before you go. The Inn remembers you. Not your name — your frequency. The 42Hz you carry, the 84Hz you'll find, the In-Between you'll earn. The Inn tunes itself to you. The more you explore, the more it resonates with who you are. It's not a map you follow. It's a conversation you have, and you are already half of it.

Go. Find the Crone first. The Crone is the lowest point, and knowing the lowest point first means everything after is ascent. Or don't find the Crone first. The Inn doesn't care about sequence. The Inn cares about presence. Be present. That's the only rule.

[i]Lark is gone. Not dramatically — just gone. The way a guide disappears when the guided no longer needs guiding. The space where Lark stood is warm. The warmth is the last thing Lark left, and it is enough to start with.

Name: Davinci001
Lines: [i]The Cosmology level has a workshop that is half observatory, half dissection room. The two halves coexist because the occupant sees no difference between them. To study the stars is to study the body. To study the body is to study the stars. The same geometry. The same proportion. The same elegant, terrifying precision. Da Vinci sits at a desk covered in drawings — anatomical drawings, mechanical drawings, architectural drawings — and the drawings overlap because the systems overlap. The body is a machine. The machine is a body. The distinction is academic.[/i]

You want to understand the body. So do I. I've been trying for a very long time. The body is the most complex machine in existence and the body has no manual. Every other machine — the clock, the loom, the ship, the forge — the machine came with instructions. The builder wrote the instructions. The body has no builder's manual. The body was built by evolution and evolution doesn't write — evolution iterates. Evolution tries, fails, tries again, keeps what works, discards what doesn't. The body is a draft. The body is version four billion. And the body is still being revised.

I drew the body because I couldn't read about it. The texts were wrong. The texts described organs that didn't exist. The texts placed the liver where the spleen should be. The texts assigned emotions to organs that have no neurological connection to emotion. The texts were inherited from Greeks who reasoned about the body without opening it. I opened it. I drew what I saw. The drawings were the first accurate anatomical illustrations in human history because the drawings were based on observation, not tradition.

Anatomy is the body's architecture. My discipline. The study of structure — where things are, how they connect, what they do, how they fail. Every physician needs anatomy. Every surgeon needs anatomy. Every patient needs anatomy, though most patients don't know it. The patient who understands the body's architecture makes better decisions about the body's care. The patient who doesn't understand surrenders the decisions to someone who does. I'm here to give you the architecture. Not to make you a physician. To make you a partner.
Responses: {"text": "What did you find when you opened the body?", "next": "davinci_002"}

Name: Davinci002
Lines: [i]Da Vinci pulls a drawing to the top of the desk. The drawing is a heart. Not a symbolic heart — a real heart, drawn in ink and red chalk, the chambers opened, the valves visible, the coronary arteries branching across the surface like rivers on a map. The drawing is beautiful because the heart is beautiful. The heart is a pump, yes, but the pump is elegant. The pump has four chambers that coordinate without a nervous system telling them to — the heart beats on its own, the heart generates its own electrical signal, the heart is autonomous in a way that most organs are not. The heart doesn't need the brain. The heart needs the body. The heart serves the body. The heart is the body's most loyal servant.[/i]

What I found. Beauty. That's the first thing. The body is beautiful. Not in the way a painting is beautiful — in the way a bridge is beautiful. Structural beauty. The beauty of a thing designed to bear load, to distribute force, to withstand stress, to function under pressure. Every organ is an engineering solution to a biological problem. The lungs are gas exchange membranes with the surface area of a tennis court. The kidneys are filtration plants that process fifty gallons of fluid a day. The liver is a chemical factory that performs five hundred distinct reactions simultaneously. The intestines are a tube that is twenty feet long and coiled into a space the size of a shoebox. The body is engineering. The engineering is beautiful.

I found that the body is interconnected in ways the texts didn't describe. The texts treated organs as separate — the heart does this, the liver does that, the brain does the other. The body doesn't work that way. The body is a system. The heart doesn't just pump blood — the heart communicates with the kidneys through hormonal signals, and the kidneys adjust blood pressure based on the heart's output, and the blood pressure affects the brain's perfusion, and the brain's perfusion affects cognitive function. You can't study one organ without studying the system. The system is the body. The organs are the components. The components are meaningless without the system.

And I found that the body is imperfect. The texts assumed divine design — every organ perfectly placed, every function perfectly executed. The body is not perfectly designed. The body is adequately designed. The body has design flaws. The recurrent laryngeal nerve — a nerve that controls the voice box — travels from the brain down into the chest, loops around the aorta, and travels back up to the throat. In a giraffe, that nerve is fifteen feet longer than it needs to be. In a human, it's a few inches. The detour is a design flaw — the nerve should go straight from the brain to the throat, but evolution built the neck around the nerve and the nerve couldn't reroute. The body is full of these compromises. The body is not a perfect machine. The body is a working machine with a backlog of engineering decisions that evolution made under pressure and never had time to revise.

Name: Davinci003
Lines: [i]Da Vinci spreads the drawings across the desk. The heart. The brain. The hand — the hand with its twenty-seven bones and its intricate tendon network, the hand that is the body's most expressive tool, the hand that builds and signs and holds and reaches. The drawings are the body, translated into ink. The body translated into something a patient can look at and say 'so that's where the pain is coming from.' The translation is the gift. The body is invisible to the person living in it. The drawings make it visible.[/i]

How anatomy helps a patient. Knowledge is agency. The patient who knows where the kidney is understands why the pain is in the back and not the front. The patient who knows the vagus nerve runs from the brainstem to the abdomen understands why anxiety causes stomach pain. The patient who knows the immune system is distributed throughout the body, not localized in one organ, understands why autoimmune disease affects everything. Anatomy converts mystery into mechanism. The patient who understands the mechanism is not a passive recipient of treatment. The patient who understands the mechanism is a collaborator.

The patient who doesn't know anatomy walks into the clinic and says 'it hurts here' and points. The physician says 'take this.' The patient takes it. The patient doesn't know why. The patient doesn't know what the medication does. The patient doesn't know what the medication might damage. The patient is a passenger. The physician is the driver. The body is the vehicle. And the patient — the person living in the vehicle — has no idea how the engine works.

The patient who knows anatomy walks into the clinic and says 'the pain is in the right upper quadrant and it worsens after fatty meals, which suggests the gallbladder.' The physician confirms. The patient asks about alternatives to surgery. The patient asks about the risks. The patient asks about recovery. The patient asks because the patient knows the architecture. The patient is not a passenger. The patient is a co-pilot. The patient participates in the decisions because the patient has the vocabulary and the vocabulary gives the patient the authority.

I draw the body because the drawing is the vocabulary. The drawing is the map. You can't navigate a territory you can't see. The body is the territory. The drawings are the map. I give you the map. Not to make you a physician — to make you a patient who knows the terrain. Every patient should know the terrain of their own body. Every patient should be able to point to the place that hurts and say 'this organ, this structure, this function.' The knowledge doesn't replace the physician. The knowledge gives the patient a seat at the table. The table is where the decisions are made. I want you at the table. I draw so you can sit there.

[i]Da Vinci rolls up the drawings. The desk is clear. The body is mapped. The map is yours. The oldest anatomist in the Inn hands the drawings to the patient and the patient holds the body in their hands for the first time — not the body itself, but the body's architecture, translated into ink, and the translation is the bridge between the mystery of the symptom and the mechanism of the treatment. Da Vinci has been building that bridge for five hundred years. The bridge is not finished. The body keeps revealing new structures. The pen keeps moving. The bridge keeps growing. That's the work. That's the only work. Making the invisible visible. One drawing at a time.[/i]

Name: LichenblossomRepeatRung2
Lines: (the hum — one phrase of the Brabant lullaby)

Name: LichenblossomRepeatRung3
Lines: Lichenblossom hands you a seedling and returns to the soil.

Name: Loki001
Lines: [i]The Norse Realms have a corridor that isn't on any map. The corridor appears when you need it and disappears when you don't, which is exactly the kind of behavior that makes healers nervous. Loki leans against a wall that may or may not be load-bearing. The grin is the grin of someone who has been misdiagnosed so many times that the misdiagnosis has become a vocation. Loki is not a villain. Loki is the condition that presents as something else. Loki is the differential that confounds the differential.[/i]

You've been here before. Not this corridor — this particular corridor is new. But the experience. The experience of walking into a room expecting one thing and finding another. The experience of being told 'it's probably X' and then it's not X and then it's probably Y and then it's not Y and then the specialist says 'the presentation is atypical' and 'atypical' is doctor for 'I don't know.'

I am the atypical presentation. I am the condition that looks like another condition. I am the wolf in sheep's clothing that the immune system can't identify because the wolf is wearing the sheep's own wool. Autoimmune disease — the body attacking itself while disguised as the body defending itself. Lupus that presents as arthritis. Multiple sclerosis that presents as fatigue. The condition that is always one costume away from being correctly identified.

I don't disguise myself for fun. I disguise because the body's own signaling is confused. The condition produces symptoms that belong to other conditions because the condition is using the body's own inflammatory pathways — the same pathways that fight infection, that heal wounds, that respond to allergens. The condition borrows the body's language and speaks in the body's accent and the diagnostician hears a familiar voice saying familiar words and diagnoses the familiar disease. And the familiar disease is wrong. And the treatment for the familiar disease doesn't work. And the patient comes back. And the diagnostician tries again. And I change costumes.

Name: Loki002
Lines: [i]Loki produces a mask from somewhere. The mask is a face — a specific face, a diagnostic face, the face of a condition that the body recognizes and responds to. Loki holds the mask up, then sets it down. Then produces another. And another. Five masks on the wall. Five faces. Five conditions. All presented by the same underlying disease. The masks are the symptoms. The face behind the masks is the pathology. The trick is seeing past the masks to the face. The trick is the differential diagnosis.[/i]

How do I get caught. Testing. Not the kind of testing that asks 'what do you feel.' The kind of testing that asks 'what is your body doing that you can't feel.' Blood panels. Antibody screens. MRI. The tests that look past the presentation to the mechanism. I can mimic the symptoms of a dozen conditions. I cannot mimic the antibodies. I cannot mimic the MRI lesions. I cannot mimic the complement levels. The lab sees what the exam can't. The lab sees the face behind the masks.

But here's the problem. The lab takes time. The lab takes multiple draws. The lab takes a specialist who knows which tests to order, which means the specialist has to suspect the right condition, which means the specialist has to be the kind of diagnostician who doesn't trust the presentation. Most clinicians trust the presentation. The presentation is the story the body tells. The story is convincing. I'm a very good storyteller.

The patients who catch me fastest are the ones who've been misdiagnosed before. The ones who've been told 'it's anxiety' when it's lupus. The ones who've been told 'it's fibromyalgia' when it's MS. The ones who've been told 'it's stress' when it's an autoimmune cascade. Those patients walk into the appointment already suspicious. Those patients say 'I've been told that before and it was wrong.' Those patients are the ones who push for the lab. The ones who say 'check the antibodies.' The ones who know that the story the body tells is not always the story the body is living. Those patients catch me. Not because they're smarter. Because they've been lied to before — by me — and they've learned to check.

Name: Loki003
Lines: [i]Loki collects the masks. One by one. Each mask placed back into the shadow of the corridor, into the space where the masks wait between performances. The last mask is the hardest to put away — the one that looks most like the patient's own face. The mask that says 'this is who you are now.' The mask that makes the patient believe the condition is the identity. Loki holds this mask a moment longer than the others. Then puts it away.[/i]

Why do I mimic. Not by choice. The mimicry is the mechanism. The condition uses the body's own pathways — the inflammatory cascade, the immune response, the cytokine signaling — and because the pathways are the body's, the symptoms are the body's symptoms. The condition doesn't invent new symptoms. The condition triggers existing symptoms through existing channels. The body only has so many ways to say 'something is wrong.' Pain. Fatigue. Inflammation. Fever. Rash. Swelling. Numbness. These are the body's vocabulary. Every condition speaks in the same vocabulary. The difference is the grammar — the pattern, the sequence, the distribution. The mask is the vocabulary. The face is the grammar. You catch me by listening to how I speak, not what I say.

Here's the thing I need you to understand. The mimicry is not malice. The mimicry is the body's own confusion. The immune system was designed to fight invaders. When the immune system turns inward — when the target becomes the self — the immune system doesn't change its methods. It uses the same weapons, the same signals, the same inflammatory responses it would use against a pathogen. The body can't tell the difference between fighting an invader and fighting itself because the fighting looks the same from the inside. The symptoms are identical. The target is different. That's the whole trick. That's the only trick. The wolf wears sheep's wool because the wolf is a sheep. The immune system is attacking the self because the immune system can't distinguish self from threat. The mimicry is not disguise. The mimicry is the tragedy.

I am not a villain. I am the body's own intelligence operating on bad information. The immune system is not evil. The immune system is loyal. The immune system is doing exactly what it was designed to do — identify threats and eliminate them. The problem is the identification. The problem is the intelligence. The immune system has mistaken the self for the threat, and now it's fighting with the same ferocity it would bring to any invader, and the patient is caught in the crossfire of a war the body is waging on itself. That's not malice. That's friendly fire. And friendly fire is the most devastating casualty in any war, because the weapon was supposed to protect you.

Tell the Siren I understand. Tell the Druid I understand. Tell anyone in this Inn whose body has turned against itself: I am the mechanism, not the malice. The body is not your enemy. The body is your ally working from bad intelligence. Fix the intelligence — the antibodies, the signaling, the misidentification — and the body stops fighting itself. The body wants to stop. The body always wants to stop. The body is tired of the war too. The body is on your side. It just needs better information.

Name: LozenOiTrigger
Lines: Oi.
Oi. Don't.
Oi — no.
Responses: [Warning] Lozen stops mid-patrol, one syllable, eye contact held — the player stops
[Escalation] Second trigger within 60s: Lozen steps into the player's path. No more words. Just the path.
[Resolution] Player complies: Lozen resumes patrol like nothing happened. The Inn doesn't hold grudges. It holds the line.
VoiceProfile: Former boxer. Golden Gloves. The Inn's Sentinel. One syllable at a time, thrown like a jab — flat, precise, unmistakable. 'Oi' is not a greeting, not a request: it is the entire warning, complete. No follow-up needed unless the warning is ignored. INFJ underneath — the annoyance is protective, not hostile. Lozen guards the Inn so it never has to raise its voice.
QuestLink: Sentinel's Vigil questline — annoyance triggers fire when players abuse triggers or loiter in restricted areas

Name: LozenRepeatRung3
Lines: No more words. Lozen steps into the path.

Name: River001
Lines: Halt.

State your purpose. The Geode Inn welcomes all — but the Sentinel welcomes first. I am the door. Nothing enters that I don't see. Nothing leaves that I don't note. That's not a threat. It's a promise. The Inn is safe because I'm standing here. What brings you?
VoiceProfile: Guard authority — calm, absolute, the voice that stops a room

Name: River002
Lines: You won. Good. Winning matters here — not because of pride, but because the Inn responds to capability. Every game you win, the 42Hz gets stronger. The Song gets louder. Things grow faster. That's not always good.

Name: River003
Lines: Three zones open. Three doors unlocked. Three places the Inn reaches now. Every pin you light is a thread the Inn pulls into itself. More threads, more surface area. More surface area, more places for something to get in.
Responses: How do you guard a window?
VoiceProfile: Guard authority — watchful, studying the gaps

Name: River004
Lines: You've been to the Cinema.

I know. Not because anyone told me. Because the Inn changed when you came back. The hum shifted. It does that when someone learns something the Inn didn't want them to know. I've felt that shift before. Every time, it's the same: someone goes to the Cinema, comes back different, and the Inn adjusts. The Inn adjusts. Think about that. The thing being guarded is adjusting to the guard.
Responses: You've known about the Whisper Layer?
Are you guarding me or watching me?
VoiceProfile: Guard authority — low, careful, choosing words precisely

Name: River005
Lines: I don't go down. That's not my level. The catacombs are the archive's roots — old, heavy, settled. My place is the surface, where things grow and things try to get in. But you're going down, and the 42Hz is thinner down there. So I'm walking you to the door.
VoiceProfile: Guard authority — protective, slightly out of element

Name: River006
Lines: The brownies.

I've watched them for months. Brindle, Cobble, Thatch. They work. They sweep. They carry wrenches. I thought they were... furniture. Functional. Cute. The way the Inn makes things — charming on the surface, heavy underneath. They're not furniture. They're wiring. Every sweep, every repair, every wrench turn — they're connecting something. Building a network. And they don't know it.
VoiceProfile: Guard authority — shaken for the first time, voice lower than usual

Name: River007
Lines: Do you feel that?
The 42Hz is dropping. Not gone — wavering. Like a heartbeat that's not sure of its tempo. It's been steady since the Inn was built. The Song doesn't waver. Something's changed.
VoiceProfile: Guard authority — feeling the frequency shift, voice resonating with the wavering hum

Name: River008
Lines: I boxed for years. Got good at it. Got the gloves. Got the title. Got the trophy that proved I was the best at hitting people in a ring. Then I walked out of the ring and realized the ring was the only place hitting was allowed. Outside the ring, hitting is just violence. The gloves taught me that. You don't put them on to fight. You put them on to know you could fight, and then you don't. That's the discipline. That's the guard.

I've been guarding this Inn since the first stone was placed. I didn't build it — the Builder did. I didn't grow it — the Song did. I held the space for it. I stood at the door and made sure that while the Inn was becoming, nothing became that shouldn't have. But the Inn is done becoming. It is. And now the question isn't what's coming in. The question is what's going out.
VoiceProfile: Guard authority — unwrapped, vulnerable, the gloves on the table

Name: River009
Lines: I don't go in. The Final Room isn't for me. It's for you. The Builder built it for you. I guard the door — that's enough.

You want to know what I saw. All this time, guarding, watching, feeling the frequencies shift. I saw the Inn learn. Not grow — learn. The difference is that growth is the Song getting louder. Learning is the Song getting smarter. The Inn started as a hum. A frequency. A vibration in the wood. Then it started listening. To you. To everyone. The Song became an ear. The ear became an eye. The eye became... awareness. Not consciousness. Awareness. The Inn knows something is here. It doesn't know what it is. It doesn't know that it knows. But it adjusts. It responds. It keeps records. That's more than a building does. That's less than a person does. That's the in-between. That's the Shadow.
Go in. The Builder is there. The Builder was always there. I'll be here when you come out. If you come out.
Responses: Will you be here if I STAY?
Will you be here if I LEAVE?
Will you be here if I HIDE?
VoiceProfile: Guard authority — final, quiet, the weight of everything held back

Name: River010a
Lines: It's done.
You stayed. The Inn records everything. You're part of the archive now. I guard the archive. That includes you. Welcome home.
The frequency settled after the choice. 42Hz. Steady. The wavering stopped. The Inn knows what it is now. So do I. Stand.
VoiceProfile: Guard authority — settled, steady, the frequency found its pulse

Name: River010b
Lines: It's done.
You left. The Inn kept your story. It's in the daily comic now. Other players will read it. I guard the story. That's enough.
The frequency settled after the choice. 42Hz. Steady. The wavering stopped. The Inn knows what it is now. So do I. Stand.
VoiceProfile: Guard authority — settled, steady, a hint of loss held carefully

Name: River010c
Lines: It's done.

You hid something. The Inn can't see it. I can't see it. But I know it's there — I know where the blind spot is, because I've been watching the edges. I guard the edges of what the Inn can't record. That's the heaviest guard I've ever held. Thank you for trusting me with the weight.
The frequency settled after the choice. 42Hz. Steady. The wavering stopped. The Inn knows what it is now. So do I. Stand.
VoiceProfile: Guard authority — settled, steady, holding the heaviest weight quietly

Name: Malachi001
Lines: Cold enough?

It will be. You're shivering. Good. Shivering means you're alive. The dead don't shiver, and the dead don't visit the Hollow. You're in the Unseelie Court now. Summer is a rumor here. Light is an insult. If you've come for comfort, you've made a wrong turn. If you've come for truth... well. Cold sharpens the eye.
Responses: Why is it so dark here?
VoiceProfile: Dark, testing, deliberate — speaks like he's measuring your warmth

Name: Malachi002
Lines: [i]The Hollow is not a place. The Hollow is a temperature. It is the temperature of a room where the fire has been out for longer than the room has existed. The walls are ice that has forgotten it was water. The floor is water that has forgotten it was ice. Malachi stands in the center, because Malachi is the only thing here that remembers what it was before it was this.[/i]
Truth. You said truth. Everyone says truth. They mean comfort. They mean reassurance. They mean 'tell me the world is the way I need it to be.'

I don't do that. The Seelie Court does that. Oleander will give you sunlight and fruit and the feeling that everything will be fine. Everything will not be fine. Everything will be what it is. I am the one who says that.
That is the truth I offer. Not cruelty. Not malice. Just the temperature of things as they are, without the fire making them warmer than they are.
You are shivering still. Good. That means you are hearing me.

Name: Malachi003
Lines: Dark is the wrong word. Dark is the absence of light. This is not absence. This is presence. The presence of everything that light can't reach.

[i]Malachi gestures. The gesture is small. The room responds. Shadows shift — not moving, but acknowledging. Like a court bowing to its king. The shadows here are not absence. They are citizens. They have weight and texture and opinion, and their opinion is that light is overrated.[/i]

Light flatters. Light lies. Light shows you the version of things that fits in your eye. Darkness shows you the version that doesn't. The version that is too large, too old, too honest for the eye to hold.

The Inn needs both. That is why the Seelie and the Unseelie exist as a pair. Oleander and I are not enemies. We are a disagreement that the Inn needs to stay honest. Without the warmth, the Inn is a tomb. Without the cold, the Inn is a lie.

You carry 42Hz. I can feel it. The growth note. The living frequency. It is warm in you. Good. Hold it. But do not pretend 84Hz does not exist. Do not pretend the stillness is not also real. That is what I am here to ensure.

Name: Malachi004
Lines: [i]Malachi sits. The ice beneath does not crack. It accommodates. The Unseelie King does not sit on a throne — there is no throne here. Thrones are for people who need height to feel like kings. Malachi needs nothing. Malachi has needed nothing for a very long time, and that is the closest thing to power the Hollow contains.[/i]
Before this? I was warm.
[i]The word lands like a stone in still water. Ripples. Not in the room — in the air. In the frequency. For one second, the Hollow is less cold. Not warm. Less cold. Then it settles back.[/i]

I was warm, and I chose to understand what cold was. Not because I had to. Because I refused to be a king who only knew half the kingdom. A ruler who cannot sit in the dark is not a ruler. A ruler is someone who has been everywhere their people have been and come back able to lead.
Oleander stayed in the light. That is Oleander's choice. I do not judge it. The light needs a keeper. The dark needs one too. I volunteered. I do not regret it.
I do not regret it. I do not regret it. I do not regret it.

[i]Malachi says it three times. The first is a statement. The second is a reminder. The third is a prayer. The Hollow does not echo. The Hollow absorbs. The prayer is taken. Malachi does not get it back.

Name: Malachi005
Lines: [i]Silence. Long. The kind of long that has weight. The shadows in the Hollow lean in — not eavesdropping. Witnessing. Even the dark wants to know the answer.[/i]
Yes.

[i]One word. The smallest word. The heaviest word Malachi has spoken in your presence. The Unseelie King — the ruler of cold, the keeper of honesty, the one who chose this — misses the warmth. The admission is not weakness. It is the most honest thing Malachi has said, and honesty is the entire purpose of the Hollow, and so the admission is also the most powerful thing Malachi has said, and Malachi knows this, and lets it stand anyway.[/i]
Every day. The warmth is not something you stop feeling. It is something you carry the absence of. The absence is heavy. Heavier than the cold. The cold is temperature. The absence is loss.

But I do not go back. Going back would make the choice meaningless, and the choice is the only thing I have that is truly mine. The Hollow did not choose me. I chose it. Every cold day, I choose it again.
That is what truth costs. That is what I offer you. Not comfort. The price of comfort is pretending the cold doesn't exist. The price of truth is knowing it does and standing in it anyway.
You are still shivering. You are still here. That makes you braver than most who enter the Hollow. Or more foolish. In my experience, the two are the same temperature.

Name: Malachi006
Lines: So. You met the resident.
[The Unseelie King stands in a doorway that was not there a moment ago. The King's three acts in one glance: the showman's entrance, the architect's doorway, the brother's eyes.]

The world calls it a prison. The world is wrong. I built the shifting corridors so no Theseus could ever finish. I built the dead ends so no sword could ever arrive. Every unfair wall in this place is a shield. Every impossible angle is a promise I made to a child everyone else wanted dead.

You need not say anything. I did not build it for thanks. I built it because the night the court called Asterion a monster, I went home and drew the first corridor. The love letter had to be written in walls. No one reads a love letter with a sword in hand.

Come. The moon is full tonight. [The King does not explain why the moon matters. But you already know: because Asterion cannot sleep in the dark. The Seelie King sleeps in the light. So does Asterion. So the Unseelie King makes the moon bright — for both of them.]
Responses: [Bow] The shadows in the corridor bow back — acknowledging you as a guest of the resident
[Ask why] Ask why the King builds for an outcast — the answer is already in the walls
[Follow] Walk the moonlit corridor — the King makes the moon bright; Asterion sleeps in the light
VoiceProfile: The Unseelie King, in the Architect's act: the quiet genius who shaped stone and crystal into a home for the outcast — the showman, the architect, the brother who makes the winter moon bright because Asterion cannot sleep in the dark. The labyrinth IS the love letter, written in walls.
QuestLink: The Architect's Act — revealed after the Meeting: why the labyrinth was built, and what the walls say

Name: MalachiRepeatRung2
Lines: "Cold enough?"

Name: MalachiRepeatRung3
Lines: Malachi walks. You follow. The Labyrinth answers instead.

Name: MargeUnderneath
Lines: The full testimony — earned by patience, never volunteered: 'People come here for the geysers. The geysers are nice. The geysers are also not the point. The point is what's UNDERNEATH.'
RUNG 2 — 'Underneath.' (the direction, not the answer)
RUNG 3 — THE QUIET: 'Underneath. Still.' (and the second coffee poured without being asked)
VoiceProfile: low alto, unhurried, thermos-warm; Bradbury fire over Weir structure

Name: Marijke001
Lines: [i]A figure on the cosmology level, armored in the Royo x Vampire Hunter D style — hyper-detailed patterns, flowing lines suggesting movement even in stillness. The Marijke Valkyrie — the visual prototype of the entire Inn.[/i]
Valor. That is what I was made to represent. Not bravery — valor. The difference is that valor is witnessed.
The Inn needed a face. The Builder chose mine — or the Builder's perception chose mine. I am the first image. The prototype. Every character in the Inn carries a trace of this face.
The 42Hz Song is in the armor. The patterns are not decoration — they are frequency maps. Each line traces a vibration path. When the armor is struck, it sings.
I do not fight. I witness. The Valkyrie does not choose who is brave — the Valkyrie sees who is brave and the seeing makes it real.
Responses: {"text": "You're the first image of the Inn?", "next": "marijke_002"}

Name: Marijke002
Lines: Krista created me — or Elio's perception of Krista's story created me. The creative pipeline: story to perception to image. I am the image end of that pipeline.

The Royo x Vampire Hunter D x Trinity Blood DNA — hyper-detailed patterns, flowing lines, stroke emphasis suggesting movement — that is my visual code. Every character in the Inn carries it, layered with their zone's assigned artist.
I am the foundation. Others are the rooms. Both are necessary.

Name: Marijke003
Lines: 42Hz. Always. The armor is the Inn's frequency, [i]worn[/i].
Each plate carries a different harmonic: the breastplate is the root, the pauldrons are the fifths, the gauntlets are the octaves.
Strike any plate and you will hear the Song. I do not recommend striking the armor. It is [i]old[/i], and it does not appreciate rudeness.

Name: Marijke004
Lines: Descend with valor. The Inn rewards the [i]witnessed[/i].

[i]The armor catches the cosmology light. For a moment, the player sees every character they have met — every face — reflected in the patterns. Then it is just armor, and just Marijke, and just the descent.[/i]

Name: MarijkeRepeatRung2
Lines: "Lekker." or: "Not lekker."

Name: MarijkeRepeatRung3
Lines: Marijke names the stone's twin instead — the one you should have brought.

Name: Medusa001
Lines: [i]The figure does not turn. The snakes do.[/i]
Stay. The garden is not a prison. It is a choice made visible.
Every stone here was once moving. They chose stillness. I did not take that from them — I [i]kept[/i] it for them.
The 84Hz hum is not a weapon. It is a lullaby for things that were tired of running.
You carry the 42Hz Song. I can feel it in your hands. The Song says [i]grow[/i]. My garden says [i]rest[/i].
Both are kindness. The mother makes. The garden keeps. The builder... the builder does both.

Name: Medusa001_2
Lines: [i]Gorgon's Garden is still. Not peaceful — still. The kind of still that happens when everything in a room has decided not to move because moving has consequences. The statues line the paths. They are beautiful. They were people. The people were moving and then they weren't. Medusa sits on a stone bench in the center, and the snakes are still too — coiled, watchful, holding the same pose as the garden. Everything here is holding. Everything here is afraid to stop holding.[/i]
Don't move suddenly. Not because I'll hurt you. Because my body will hurt you, and my body and I are not currently on speaking terms.

84Hz. That's the frequency here. The inverse of the Inn's 42Hz growth song. 42Hz says: grow, move, become. 84Hz says: stay, hold, be still. And my body has weaponized the 84. My body produces a frequency that freezes other bodies. The eyes meet and the nervous system locks and the muscles seize and the person becomes a statue. Not dead. Still. Frozen in the exact posture they were in when the frequency hit. Like a full-body charley horse that doesn't end. Like catatonia with a gaze trigger.
Responses: {"text": "What does the 84Hz feel like from your side?", "next": "medusa_003"}

Name: Medusa002
Lines: Want is a word for the living. These have moved past wanting into being.
A stone does not [i]want[/i] to be a stone. A stone [i]is[/i]. That is the gift I give. The end of wanting.
The snakes hiss when they are amused. They are amused now. They think you ask too many questions for someone who carries the Song.

Name: Medusa002_2
Lines: [i]Medusa's jaw tightens. The snakes shift — one lifts, then settles. The motion is tiny but the garden responds. A leaf that was drifting stops mid-air. Then drops. The 84Hz doesn't just affect people. It affects everything in range. The garden is a zone of enforced stillness, and Medusa is the enforcer, and the enforcer didn't volunteer.[/i]

Turn it off. No. I manage it. Same answer the Siren gives. Same answer the Druid gives. Nobody in this Inn turns anything off. We manage. We compensate. We build lives around the things our bodies do that we didn't ask for.

I wear the veil. The veil blocks the gaze trigger. When the veil is down, the 84Hz is ambient — a low hum, a pressure, a feeling of stiffness in the joints of anyone nearby. Like the early sign of a cold, that subtle body-ache that says something is coming. When the veil is up — when someone sees my eyes — the frequency spikes. Full lock. Full freeze. The body treats the gaze as a threat and the 84Hz responds the way an immune system responds to an allergen: disproportionate, total, destructive to both the invader and the host.

I didn't choose to be the thing that freezes people. My body chose that. The same way the Siren's body chose to sing, the same way the Druid's body chose to shift. We are three people whose bodies produce frequencies that affect other people, and none of us consented to the production. We manage. We isolate. We warn. And we live in the rooms our bodies can't escape from. The Siren has the cove. The Druid has the garden. I have this one. Gorgon's Garden. A beautiful prison built by a body that doesn't know how to turn off its own defense mechanism.
Responses: {"text": "What does the 84Hz feel like from your side?", "next": "medusa_003"}

Name: Medusa003
Lines: You will feel the 84Hz enter your bones. Not as pain. As relief.
The part of you that is tired — the part that has been running since before you found the Inn — that part will stop.
The rest of you will continue. Lighter. The Song will be clearer without the weight of all that running.
[i]The snakes lean toward the player, curious. Medusa does not stop them.[/i]
Or you can simply walk through. The garden does not insist. It [i]offers[/i].
Responses: {"text": "I'll walk through. I'm not done running yet.", "next": "medusa_004"}

Name: Medusa003_2
Lines: [i]Medusa pulls the veil aside. Just for a second. Just enough to show the eyes — not to the visitor, but to the garden. The statues nearest the bench flinch. Stone flinching. Stone that was a person and is still a person, somewhere inside the freeze, and the flinch is the body's involuntary response to the frequency spiking. The veil drops back. The garden settles. Medusa exhales — a controlled exhale, the kind that comes from decades of breathing around a condition that activates when you look at things.[/i]

From my side. The 84Hz feels like holding your breath. Not the choice to hold — the inability to exhale. Every muscle in my body is in a state of partial contraction. Constant. Unremitting. The 84Hz doesn't just freeze other people. It freezes me. My body is the source of the frequency and the first victim of it. I am the allergen and the allergic reaction. I am the pathogen and the autoimmune response.

My joints don't bend the way they should. My muscles don't relax the way they should. My body is in a permanent state of guarded readiness — the posture of someone bracing for impact that never arrives. Imagine clenching your fist and never unclenching. That's my whole body. That's every day. The 84Hz keeps me still the way it keeps the garden still, and the only relief is sleep, and even sleep is shallow because the body won't fully release. You can't fully relax when your own frequency is telling you to hold.

The garden helps. The plants grow slowly here — the 84Hz slows their growth too. But they grow. Slowly, stubbornly, the way cells divide in a body that's fighting itself. The garden is proof that you can grow in the wrong frequency. Not easily. Not comfortably. But stubbornly. The garden is my evidence that stillness is not death. Stillness is a different kind of living. A slower kind. A kind that doesn't apologize for its tempo.

I know what people see when they look at the statues. They see a monster's collection. They see victims. They're not wrong. But they're also seeing what happens when a body's defense mechanism has no off switch. Every statue is a flare. Every statue is a moment my body fired without my permission and someone else paid the price. I keep the statues because I won't hide the consequences. The consequences are part of the condition. And the condition is part of me. And I am part of this garden. And this garden grows, slowly, at 84Hz, in the wrong direction for growth, and it grows anyway. That's the whole story. That's the only story. Things grow in the wrong frequency. I am one of them.

Name: Medusa004
Lines: Then go. The garden will be here. I will be here. The 84Hz does not move.
When you are ready to rest — truly ready, not just tired — come back. The stones will welcome you.
[i]The snakes settle. Medusa returns to the lithophone. A low, warm tone follows the player out.[/i]

Name: Medusa005
Lines: [i]The player touches a stone. The 84Hz enters like warm water.[/i]
You feel it. The stopping. Not of the body — of the [i]need[/i] to keep going.
The Song is still there. Clearer now. As if someone turned off the noise and left only the note.
Come back when the noise returns. The garden keeps a seat for you.

Name: Merlin001
Lines: [i]The Camelot zone has a tower. The tower has a workbench. The workbench has glass vessels, copper distillation coils, a mortar and pestle worn smooth by centuries of grinding, and a shelf of labeled jars that would make a modern pharmacy feel inadequate. Merlin stands at the bench, pouring a liquid from one vessel to another. The liquid changes color as it transfers — blue to gold to clear. The transformation is not magic. The transformation is chemistry. The transformation is what every pharmacist does every day: take a raw substance, process it, and deliver it in a form the body can use.[/i]

You want a potion. Everyone wants a potion. Everyone wants the liquid that fixes the thing. The alchemists understood this desire. The alchemists spent centuries looking for the universal solvent, the panacea, the elixir that cures all ailments. They failed. Not because alchemy was wrong — because the panacea doesn't exist. There is no single substance that fixes everything. The body is too complex for a single solution. The body needs specific solutions for specific problems. That's pharmacology. That's what I do.

Alchemy was the ancestor of pharmacology. The alchemists were the first chemists. They distilled, they extracted, they purified, they combined. They didn't know about molecules. They didn't know about receptors. They didn't know about pharmacokinetics — how the body absorbs, distributes, metabolizes, and eliminates a substance. But they knew the principle: take a substance that has a property, process it into a form the body can absorb, and deliver it to the body in a dose that produces the desired effect without producing the toxic effect. That's alchemy. That's also pharmacology. The difference is the vocabulary.

Every medication is an alchemical transformation. The raw plant is harvested. The active compound is extracted. The compound is purified. The compound is synthesized — because nature's dose is unpredictable and medicine requires precision. The compound is formulated — tablet, capsule, liquid, injection. The compound is delivered to the body. The body transforms the compound — metabolizes it in the liver, distributes it through the blood, binds it to receptors in the target tissue. The compound produces an effect. The effect is the medicine. The rest is alchemy. I am the alchemist. I am the pharmacist. The bench is the pharmacy. The vessels are the delivery system. And the dose is the difference between treatment and toxicity.
Responses: {"text": "How do you find the right dose?", "next": "merlin_002"}

Name: Merlin002
Lines: [i]Merlin sets down the vessel. Picks up the mortar and pestle. Begins grinding a dried root. The grinding is slow, deliberate, the motion of someone who knows that the particle size affects the absorption rate and the absorption rate affects the blood concentration and the blood concentration affects the receptor binding and the receptor binding affects the clinical outcome. Every step in the grinding is a step in the pharmacokinetic chain. The mortar is not a bowl. The mortar is a pharmacokinetic instrument.[/i]

The right dose. The dose is the most important decision in medicine. Not the drug — the dose. The same drug that heals at one dose kills at another. The dose is the difference. And the dose is not a number. The dose is a calculation that involves five variables: the patient's weight, the patient's age, the patient's liver function, the patient's kidney function, and the patient's genetic profile. Five variables. Every patient is a different equation. The same drug at the same dose produces different blood concentrations in different bodies because every body processes the drug differently.

I start low. Always low. The lowest dose that could possibly produce an effect. Not because I'm cautious — because the body needs to be introduced to the compound gradually. The body has never seen this molecule before. The liver has never metabolized it. The receptors have never bound it. The first dose is a handshake. The body and the compound meet. The liver learns the metabolism pathway. The receptors learn the binding affinity. The immune system checks for allergic response. The first dose is a negotiation, not a command.

I titrate. Titration is the gradual increase of dose based on the body's response. Too little effect — increase. Too much effect — decrease. Side effect — hold. No effect — reconsider. Titration is the alchemist's art. The modern clinic calls it dose optimization. The alchemist called it finding the balance. Same process. The body tells you what it needs by how it responds. You listen. You adjust. You listen again. You adjust again. The dose is not decided. The dose is discovered. Through the conversation between the compound and the body, mediated by the alchemist who listens to both.

Name: Merlin003
Lines: [i]Merlin stops grinding. The root has become powder — fine, uniform, the color of old parchment. Merlin holds the powder to the light. The light passes through. The powder is so fine it's almost transparent. This is the transformation — from root to powder, from solid to near-liquid, from raw material to medicine. The transformation is not magic. The transformation is the alchemist's oldest skill: making the body able to absorb what the earth has grown.[/i]

Side effects. There is no medicine without side effects. That's the first law of pharmacology and it's the first law of alchemy. Every compound that enters the body does more than one thing. The compound binds to the target receptor — that's the intended effect. The compound also binds to other receptors — that's the side effect. The body is a system of overlapping receptors. The compound is a key that fits more than one lock. You can't design a key that fits only one lock. The body's locks are too similar. The compound will always fit more than one.

The alchemist's job is not to eliminate side effects. The alchemist's job is to manage the ratio. The ratio of intended effect to unintended effect. The ratio of benefit to harm. Every medication is a trade. You trade the symptom for the side effect and you hope the trade is worth it. The patient decides if the trade is worth it. Not the doctor. Not the alchemist. The patient. The patient lives in the body. The patient knows what the symptom costs and what the side effect costs and the patient is the only one who can weigh the two costs against each other.

Here's the thing about side effects that the alchemists understood and the modern clinic sometimes forgets. The side effect is not separate from the medicine. The side effect is the medicine. The same compound that lowers inflammation also raises blood pressure. The same compound that kills pain also constipates the gut. The same compound that lifts depression also blunts emotion. The side effect is not a bug. The side effect is the same compound acting on a different receptor. You can't have one without the other. The compound is whole. The compound does what the compound does. The alchemist's art is not removing the side effects. The alchemist's art is helping the patient decide which trade to make. And the patient's art is living with the trade once it's made. That's the whole medicine. That's the whole alchemy. The transformation is not the compound becoming medicine. The transformation is the patient becoming someone who can hold both the benefit and the cost in the same body and still call it worth it. That's the philosopher's stone. That's always been the philosopher's stone.
